description: Source reliability hierarchy for this project. Tiers are used in every case file. Tier does not guarantee correctness — it ranks authority for conflict resolution.

tiers.label: Official NBA / league sources
examples: Official box scores / play-by-play on NBA.com/stats.nba.com
tiers.use: Authoritative for corrections, protest rulings, and final official values.

tiers.label: Wire reporting (AP and republication)
tiers.use: Strong corroboration; often the text behind NBA.com (AP) items.

tiers.label: Major sports media
tiers.use: Reliable for facts with named sourcing; require cross-check for sole-source claims.

tiers.label: Team beat / regional outlets
tiers.use: Good for local detail; corroborate league-level claims.

tiers.label: Secondary digital outlets
tiers.use: Usable with attribution; never the sole basis for a 'verified' core fact. Action Network betting math is its beat and cited as such.

tiers.label: Tertiary / unverified
tiers.use: Leads only. Facts sourced here MUST be flagged unverified and re-corroborated before use.

authoritative_references.note: Rule 5, Section I(8): 'If there is a discrepancy in the score and it cannot be resolved, the running score shall be official.' Foundation for score-conflict resolution.
Rule 13: successful 2-pt/3-pt rulings are reviewable within strict timing windows (next-stoppage rules). Cited for procedure context.
Replay trigger explainer for 2-vs-3 reviews since 2008-09.
Elias has been the NBA's official statistician since 1970-71. Corrections flow through the league + Elias pipeline.

ESPN documents three distinct mechanisms: (1) live-scoring updates as better league data arrives, (2) post-game NBA adjustments, (3) ESPN feed-data corrections. This taxonomy is adopted by the monitor to classify detections.
